utterances.text: So, you were invited during the Muslim Croat conflict. Was there ever a decision adopted to start to wage a war against the Muslims there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, formally such a decision was never adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am not speaking about formally -- were you present on such occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no formal decision adopted, but it is very clear that such a decision was implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am speaking -- it is very clear that the war came about, but I do not know if it was the formal decision or not, but was such a decision ever adopted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, such a decision was never adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you were in the HDZ leadership during the Muslim Croat conflict. Was there ever a decision reached to ethnically cleanse the Muslim population in the territories controlled by the Croats and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I must tell you that there was discussion in such meetings about the situation in certain municipalities and I was sitting next to Pero Markovic, the mayor of Capljina, at one of such meetings. I asked him, "What is the situation like between the Muslims and Croats in your city?" He said, "There is no situation in our place -- we have no Muslims left, because we just cleansed them all."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: He said that of Capljina. Was ever a decision taken in these meetings to go into the ethnic cleansing of Muslims from certain regions -- to burn down their houses; was there such a decision taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Such a decision was implemented, and if you will recall, in the Croatian Parliament, a representative who visited these territories controlled by the Croatian army, that is the HVO, stated that he was surprised by the misinformation that seeped into the public. For instance, that a mosque was burned down in Livno and he said, "I was in this mosque and I can tell you that it was not burned down and I chased out some sheep and some goats from this mosque personally, because I could not see that they would be in a place of worship, so I could tell, if sheep and goats were there, people could not have attended it."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr Mesic, I would like you to answer my questions directly -- the way it is appropriate for this institution. I asked you a direct question: when people from the BHDZ would come to these meetings, was there ever a decision taken to ethnically cleanse the territories controlled by the HVO. Have you heard of a decision, were you present there, did you take part in such decision taking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not and such a decision was not formally taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The English -- the translation says that it was not formally taken, such a decision, but did you hear that somebody informally said, "Let us do this, we will not put it down as a decision". Was that -- did that happen at one of the meetings with Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since representatives from various parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina came to these meetings, where obviously there were movements of the Muslim population, and let us set aside things that were happening in Mostar, it was clear to me that somehow such policies were implemented, sort of by way of sidelines, but officially it was always held that Bosnia consisted of three constituent populations, and so on -- let me not go into all the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: These meetings were not public meetings -- these were internal meetings. The contents of such meetings were not revealed except what was decided to be publicised, but what I am asking you is did somebody say, like Tudjman, "Let us go and cleanse the Muslims from the Travnik territory", for instance. Did you hear some such thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the Muslim leaders come to Zagreb frequently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was only through Zagreb that they could reach the rest of the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, you saw them around there frequently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You characterised Perinovic, Kljujic and Brkic as persons who advocated the whole and unified Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How do you explain the fact that Tudjman and you said that he had a significant if not paramount influence in Bosnia -- how did he agree that such persons would be elected to the positions that they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I guess they did not want to implement the policies that were asked of them, and so at first, for Perinovic they said that his ancestors were Serb, so he was not to be trusted and then Kljujic, that he was married to a Muslim, and that he was going to implement Alija Izetbegovic policies, and for Brkic, he was too moderate and also was not fully acceptable for the realisation of the Croatian policies in Bosnia, and so they arrived at Mate Boban, for whom Tudjman said he was the only person who understands his policy in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. These are all the reasons why to relieve someone of the duties, but how come that Tudjman accepted appointments of three separate persons who are not implementing his policies -- how do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have tried to explain that Tudjman's policy towards Bosnia also shifted in time; from the time when he also was advocating the unified Bosnia up until Karadordevo -- after that he evolves in a certain way because he was convinced that Milosevic would succeed in breaking up Bosnia and that it would benefit him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. We will now move on to the replacement of Kljujic. In the examination-in-chief you said, "I was put in charge of relieving Kljujic on behalf of the HVO." This was a meeting of the executive board; could you have effected his removal without his own will?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I could not, because at that time the faction which advocated the unified Bosnia and Herzegovina prevailed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that you came from Zagreb in order to remove Kljujic. I would like to play a videotape, so please can we play it? This is videotape number 1. It is very short. I would also ask the interpreter to interpret, if they can -- if not, I would like to replay it in order to get most of it. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: (translating videotape). "Question: What is it about the division of Bosnia-Herzegovina? I do not know about the meeting in Siroki Brijeg, but you said Bosnia-Herzegovina has to stay whole, not only because the international community wants it but it is also in the interests of Croats in Bosnia? Answer: We always had the policy that the borders were inviolable, that they cannot be changed. This concerns Croatia as well as the other countries. However, I must say that the leadership of Bosnia-Herzegovina waited too long, that the moment of decision was when Croatia decided to go alone, because it is the best way to protect its own interests when it was clear that Serbia is not accepting the confederal concept proposed by Slovenia and Croatia, for all units of the former Yugoslavia. I think that the BH was late. I think that it was because the SDA leadership believed that they could eschew this pressure, that there would be no war. Now we see that Bosnia is occupied; there is the largest concentration of soldiers in Europe and equipment right now, and it is very difficult now for Bosnia to achieve what Croatia and Slovenia have already achieved. So I believe that this referendum is a bit too late. But, as the saying says, it is better late than never, and so I think that it should go ahead, so that Bosnia should become independent so that the Serb army would leave the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and so that the Bosniak can proceed on its own independent way, and all the advantages which it has with close cooperation with Croatia can come to be." (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please can we play the second segment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The only request I have is if counsel could identify the dates of these film clips it would be helpful to me and to the court, and perhaps to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that Mr Nobilo has to give all the information -- the identifying elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We are going to try to ask Mr Mesic -- this was a "Picture on Picture" programme -- this is when you came back from Siroki Brijeg after the removal of Kljujic. Do you remember this interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, but I do not recall the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But do you accept that this was immediately after the removal of Kljujic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I do recall the broadcast, but I do not know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you recall the date when Kljujic was relieved of his duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Mr President, we cannot give you the exact date. This is one day after Kljujic was relieved of his duty in Siroki Brijeg. Maybe subsequently we will be able to provide a date. Please, the next segment. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: (translating videotape). "Not only the sovereignty of people as people but also the sovereignty of a territory, because if the SDS claims that the sovereignty extends to where only 5 per cent of Serbs live, that is an imperial policy as dictated by Milosevic, which is something that Karadzic only implements -- he is a small puppet. However, Croatian people cannot just react to challenges -- it has to spell out its own position, both in the entire Bosnia-Herzegovina and in the territory that it occupies. Question: Speaking about Milosevic and Karadzic, oftentimes the parallel is made between Kljujic and the congressional leadership, and they say he had to leave because he would not implement? Answer: No, nobody says that he had to resign. It was at the very end of the discussion that he decided to resign. Nobody asked for him to step down. We are a Croatian community, so we are democratic." (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: With respect to the first segment, were you at the time expressing the position of the Croatian Democratic Union?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So these were not just your own personal views, but also the positions of the Party you belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You told us here that your task was to replace Kljujic, but on Croatian television you said that nobody replaced Kljujic. There is a slight difference between those two statements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there is no difference. You did not understand me. No-one, at the meeting, required the dismissal of Kljujic at that meeting, and I came with Tudjman's instructions to have him removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So somebody did ask for his removal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the meeting, no-one did, but I came with Tudjman's request for him to be removed. What do you think -- do you think I could have said on television I went there with instructions to remove Kljujic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does that mean that you do not always tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but at the time I could not have said that, because political circumstances would not allow it. I always tell the truth, but if the pressure is such as it was at the time, then I could not go into the details. Political considerations would not allow me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, if I understood you well -- please correct me -- depending on whether you will go into all the details or not, the complete truth or part of the truth, depends on political circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Clearly, at the time, as the executive secretary of the Party, I could not state for the benefit of the public that President Tudjman required the removal of Kljujic, but I did tell Kljujic that in confidence -- I told him -- and you can check -- "my task is first to persuade you to resign" and he said, "Is this the explicit request of Tudjman?" I said, "Yes, explicitly", but I added, "I see that people here support you, that it is not possible to replace you here, maybe only a third would vote in favour of that, so I will go back to Zagreb and say that you won the support of the meeting and what will happen after that, we will see". However, even after this -- first he said he was sick, and then he said that he believed that Tudjman could remove him in one way or another and then he left, he went to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: One further question: if political circumstances affected your decision to speak the whole truth or not, what about the political circumstances today -- how do they affect your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are wrong. This was not a question of the truth -- I told the truth. No-one at the meeting there -- there -- will you please repeat what I am saying -- no-one over there asked for Kljujic to resign, so will you repeat that. I said "over there" and nobody asked me whether Tudjman had asked for his replacement, so it was not my duty to say even that it was Tudjman's request.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In any event, what we saw now, these two clips, was that indeed an interview with you -- did you indeed say what you said on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Was that me?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Are those your words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Surely I can recognise myself, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But we need to authenticate the evidence and that is why I have to ask you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did recognise myself in this clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So could please the Registrar have these tapes translated and of course that is our next Defence exhibit. Could you please give us a number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr Harmon, we will consider these have been identified by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr President. The only thing is I renew my request that a date on this tape be provided to the Prosecutor's Office. Second of all, Mr President, I would request that any transcript of this tape, fully translated, in English, be provided to the Prosecutor's Office before Mr Mesic retires from his testimony, so if there are any discrepancies between the translation and the tape, I would have an opportunity to ask Mr Mesic about the substance of that tape. I do not understand the tape, I rely on the interpreters, but I would like to have hard copy in front of me and I would like to be able to review it with Mr Mesic, if the occasion requires so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We do not object if Mr Mesic is going to stay for a while, but if the Registry is unable to do that quickly, there should be no problems in calling the witness to come back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps tomorrow morning when there is no hearing, it could be translated. It seems rather long and it seems legitimate for the Prosecutor to want to have translations but he can use it for his right to re-examination. Although, of course, we do compliment the interpreters on their work, but I think that a written text in English would be good. I do not dare ask for one in French, but at least one in English.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We will take care of that. We will take care of getting a translation for tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We are going to break and we will start at 3 o'clock, because at 2.00 or 2.30 there is a status conference for a different case. I see Mr Harmon has another question. We do agree about the identification. I think it can only be identified once -- identified totally once we know what was the date of that interview.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D98.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The other request I have, if counsel is going to use documents that are in the Croatian language, and then provide them to me, they are of little utility for me because I cannot read them. If he has some documents he intends to introduce and show this witness during his cross-examination, I request that he submit those to the translation department so they can be translated into English, and when he submits a copy to me, I can read it, the translation, and I can use it effectively.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr President, we have had this kind of discussion many times. We have a lot of documents. Mr Mesic is a public figure. All the things he said here, he said earlier on, we claim in a different way. We agree, but in that case, we must suspend the cross-examination until everything is translated, and then call back Mr Mesic, or, in order to save time, we will proceed in the way we have so far. I do not intend to produce whole pages or whole articles, but only passages and in that way we can expedite the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I do not intend to be presumptuous in telling the Defence how to proceed with its case. Quite clearly, they have had Mr Mesic's testimony for a considerable period of time. They have had it since 6 May. They have prepared this examination by collecting these documents which are relevant. I do not ask the court to suspend the testimony of Mr Mesic, but perhaps efforts could be taken at this late juncture to submit those to translation so that the translation section can provide, or make efforts to provide those documents to me. They have had a clear eye on what questions they intend to use and what documents they intend to use to impeach, or attempt to impeach Mr Mesic's testimony. It comes as no surprise -- they are not operating in the dark on these. My request is, if they do not have English translations at present, that they submit those documents, which they clearly know and intend to use, and introduce as exhibits in the cross-examination of Mr Mesic, to the translation services and that the translation services make maximal efforts to provide translations of those copies to us. I might add, Mr President, that the Prosecutor's Office also endeavours to provide to both the court and the Defence translations in English and French, in advance of using the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If I may speak on behalf of my colleague? We strongly object to the Prosecutor telling us, the Defence, how we should prioritise our work in our requests of the translation unit. As a side bar, ex parte, we will tell the court how many documents we have pending with the translation unit to be translated, that we are waiting for. I am not going to state that publicly. I can say Mr Nobilo has been gathering these items, including during the testimony -- he was out photocopying minutes before the testimony. We react to the testimony and we gather material. Quite frankly, this is not the Prosecutor's prerogative. He can translate everything we produce. This is his witness. He can bring him back, but he is not in a position to unilaterally impose these burdens and requirements on us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: First of all, the Prosecution is not imposing anything -- just as the Defence is not imposing anything -- not one on the other. The Tribunal decides. We have already decided what we will do with the video. If any other documents need to be provided to the translation, that should be done. We are pleased with the interpretation of the interpreters here, and in case not all of the documents are translated, you can use the interpretation of those that have been interpreted. If that is not enough, of course then Mr Mesic would be brought back. But let us not make an incident out of something where there should not be. I recall once again that if your presiding judge were to interrupt each time -- every moment of the proceedings when there was not a translation, we would have a lot of interruptions. Everybody has to do their best. We will now suspend this hearing and resume tomorrow at 3 o'clock.
